The Minister of Science and ICT may set different terms of validity up to the effective period listed in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) if an authorized person of a radio station or applicant referred to in Article 20 (2) 4 and 5 of the Act so desires. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Notwithstanding paragraph (1) 2-2, the Minister of Science and ICT (including the Korea Communications Commission that grants authorization to establish broadcasting stations under Article 34) may grant authorization with an effective period of authorization reduced by up to two years taking into account the results of evaluation under Article 10 (1) or 17 (3) of the Broadcasting Act , if deemed necessary to promote public welfare through the efficient use and management of radio waves. <Added on Jul. 26, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 18, 2018>

The Minister of Science and ICT shall give prior notice of the procedures for renewal of authorization and the fact that he or she will not be granted the renewal of authorization if he or she fails to file an application within the period for application for the renewal of authorization referred to in Article 38 (1) to each authorized person, by no later than four months before the date the effective period of authorization to establish a radio station terminates. In such cases, such prior notice may be given in writing, or by telephone, facsimile, etc. <Added on Dec. 3, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Jan. 5, 2021>
Article 37 (Effective period of approval to use radio frequencies)
The effective period of approval to use radio frequencies granted under Article 22 (1) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Radio stations referred to in subparagraphs 1 and 5 of Article 23 : 10 years;
Radio stations referred to in subparagraphs 3 and 6 of Article 23 : Five years;
Radio stations referred to in subparagraphs 2 and 4 of Article 23 : A period deemed necessary by the Minister of Science and ICT for achieving the purpose of establishing relevant radio stations.

Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where the Minister of Science and ICT deems that granting approval to use radio frequencies during the effective period referred to in paragraph (1) 1 or 2 impedes the efficient use of spectrum resources on the grounds that the allocation of radio frequencies is changed, the period necessary to achieve the purpose of approval for use is shorter than the effective period referred to in paragraph (1) 1 or 2, etc., he or she may set different terms of validity up to the terms of validity referred to in paragraph (1) 1 or 2 after consulting thereon with an applicant for approval for the use of radio frequencies. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

The Minister of Science and ICT shall give prior notice of the procedures for renewal of approval and the fact that he or she will not be granted the renewal of approval if he or she fails to file an application within the application period for the renewal of approval referred to in Article 39 to the person granted approval to use, no later than one year before the date the effective period of approval to use radio frequencies expires. In such cases, such prior notice may be given in writing, or by telephone, facsimile, etc. <Added on Dec. 3, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Jan. 5, 2021>
Article 38 (Renewal of authorization)

A person who seeks to renew authorization pursuant to Article 22 (1) of the Act shall file an application for renewal of authorization with the Minister of Science and ICT by no later than two to four months before the expiration of its effective period; provided, where the effective period of a radio station is one year, an application shall be filed by no later than two months before the expiration of such effective period; and where the effective period of a radio station is less than one year, an application shall be filed no later than one month before the expiration of such effective period. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

A person who seeks to renew authorization for a satellite broadcasting station pursuant to Article 22 (1) of the Act shall submit an application for renewal of authorization (including an electronic application form) accompanied by an installation outline and a plan for construction of radio facilities. <Added on Aug. 27, 2014>

Upon receipt of an application for renewal of authorization for a satellite broadcasting station under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT shall verify the following documents through administrative data matching pursuant to Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act ; provided, where the applicant and the person responsible for broadcast programming would not consent to the verification of the materials referred to in subparagraph 2, the Minister shall require them to submit the relevant documents: <Added on Aug. 27, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
A corporate registration certificate;
Certificates of records of family relationships of each of the representative of the corporation and the person responsible for broadcast programming.

Where an application for renewal of authorization is deemed appropriate under Article 21 (2) of the Act after examining the application, the Minister of Science and ICT shall renew such authorization; provided, where the status, etc. of the use of radio frequencies differs from those at the time an application for authorization was filed, he or she may grant authorization upon re-designating the following matters: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Aug. 27, 2014; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>
Type of radio frequencies, occupied bandwidth, and radio frequencies;
Call sign or call letters;
Antenna power;
Permissible working hours;
Certification types of operators and the fixed number of operators;
Type, configuration and gain of antennas;
Matters of broadcast and the broadcast service area in cases of a radio station for broadcasting.
Article 39 (Renewal of approval)
Article 39-2 (Procedures for reporting on establishment of radio stations)

A person who intends to report the establishment of a radio station pursuant to the former part of Article 22-2 (1) of the Act shall file a report on the establishment of a radio station (including an electronic report form) with the Minister of Science and ICT along with a summary statement of radio facilities and construction drawings (excluding a radio station referred to in Article 19-2 (1) 1 and 2 of the Act). <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where a report on the establishment of a radio station falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the reporter may submit only one copy of the report on the establishment of a radio station; provided, one copy of a summary statement of radio facilities and construction drawings shall be submitted in cases falling under subparagraph 2:

Where reports on the establishment of at least two radio stations belonging to the same type, which is portable radio equipment referred to in the main clause of Article 24 (1) 1 or the main clause of subparagraph 3 of that paragraph, are simultaneously filed;

Where reports on the establishment of at least two satellite broadcasting auxiliary stations or terrestrial broadcasting auxiliary stations established underground or within a tunnel under Article 24 (3) are simultaneously filed.

Where a person who has established a radio station pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2) intends to change the following matters pursuant to the latter part of Article 22-2 (1) of the Act, he or she shall file a report on change accompanied by construction drawings of radio facilities (excluding where matters regarding Article 31 (4) 1, 2, 4 and 8 are changed and where a radio station under Article 19-2 (1) 1 and 2 of the Act is changed) and the detailed statement of change in the radio station with the Minister of Science and ICT: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 17, 2019>
Matters referred to in Article 31 (4) 1, 2, 4 and 6 through 8;
The place to install radio facilities or where radio facilities are placed permanently (excluding cases of simplex radio stations using portable radio equipment);

Type of radio waves, occupied bandwidth, and radio frequencies (excluding where a facility-based telecommunications business entity changes radio frequencies within the bandwidth allocated to him or her pursuant to Articles 11 and 12 of the Act);
Installation of more transmitters;
Replacement of radio equipment.
Article 39-3 (Entries in certificates of reports on radio stations)

The following shall be stated in a certificate of report on a radio station issued under Article 22-2 (2) of the Act; provided, in cases of radio stations referred to in Article 24 (1), matters referred to in Article 33 (1) 4 and 11 through 15 shall be excluded: <Amended on Dec. 17, 2019>
Matters referred to in Article 33 (1) 2 through 5 and 8 through 16;
Reporting number, and date of receipt;
The place to install radio facilities or where radio facilities are placed permanently (excluding cases of simplex radio stations using portable radio equipment).

Article 33 (2) through (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the correction of a certificate of report on a radio station and the re-issuance thereof. In such cases, "certificate of authorization" shall be construed as "certificate of report"; "matter other than those prescribed in the subparagraphs of Article 31 (4)" as "matter other than those prescribed in the subparagraphs of Article 39-2 (3); and "detailed statement of change to authorized matters" as "detailed statement of change to reported matters", respectively. <Amended on Dec. 3, 2014>
Article 40 (Filing applications for authorization to succeed to status of authorized persons)

A person who intends to obtain authorization to succeed to the status of an authorized person pursuant to the main clause of, and proviso of, Article 23 (2) of the Act shall submit an application for authorization in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Science and ICT or publicly notified by the Korea Communications Commission to the Minister of Science and ICT or the Korea Communications Commission along with the following documents: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Aug. 27, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Mar. 26, 2024>
Where he or she falls under Article 23 (1) 1 of the Act: A copy of a business transfer and acquisition contract;
Where he or she falls under Article 23 (1) 2 of the Act:
A copy of a corporate merger contract;
Minutes of shareholders' plenary meeting or members' plenary meeting in which a resolution on a merger was passed and other documents verifying decisions regarding the merger;
A copy of the articles of incorporation of a corporation surviving or resulting from the merger or consolidation;
Deleted. <Mar. 26, 2024>

Upon receipt of an application for authorization paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT or the Korea Communications Commission shall verify the following documents by sharing the administrative information pursuant to Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act ; provided, where the applicant (in cases of a corporation, referring to the representative thereof) would not consent to the verification of the matters referred to in subparagraph 2 or 3, the Minister shall require him or her to submit the relevant documents: <Added on Aug. 27, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Mar. 26, 2024>
A corporate registration certificate;
A alien registration certificate issued under Article 88 of the Immigration Act (only applicable to persons falling under Article 20 (1) 1 through 3 of the Act);

A family relation certificate of the representative of the corporation (applicable only to an application for authorization to succeed to the status of the authorized person of a satellite broadcasting station).
Article 41 (Succession to status of authorized persons upon filing reports)

"Radio station prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause of Article 23 (3) of the Act means a simplex radio station or a radio station established upon filing a report thereon pursuant to Article 19-2 (1) of the Act. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013>

A person who intends to file a report on succession to the status of the authorized person pursuant to the main clause and proviso of Article 23 (3) of the Act shall file the report in the form prescribed by the Ministry of Science and ICT or the Korea Communications Commission along with documents proving the fact of succession with the Ministry of Science and ICT or the Korea Communications Commission. <Amended on Mar. 26, 2024>

Upon receipt of a report filed under paragraph (2), the Minister of Science and ICT or the Korea Communications Commission shall verify the following documents by sharing the administrative information pursuant to Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act ; provided, if the person who has filed the report (in the case of a corporation, referring to the representative) does not consent to the verification under subparagraph 2 or 3, the relevant documents shall be attached to the report: <Added on Mar. 26, 2024>
A corporate registration certificate;
A alien registration certificate issued under Article 88 of the Immigration Act (only applicable to persons falling under Article 20 (1) 1 through 3 of the Act);

A family relation certificate of the representative of the corporation (only applicable to reporting on authorization to succeed to the status of the authorized person of a satellite broadcasting station).
Article 42 (Reporting on completion of construction)
Article 42-2 (Sampling inspections)

To conduct a sampling inspection pursuant to the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 24 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "sampling inspection"), samples shall be selected (rounded up to the nearest whole number) at not less than 30/100 (hereinafter referred to as "sampling ratio") of the radio stations whose completion is filed within the period of sample collection by each jurisdiction for inspections. In such cases, detailed matters regarding the operation of the sampling inspection, such as the jurisdiction for the inspection, period of sample collection, and the sampling ratio, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Aug. 27, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

"When Presidential Decree so prescribes" in the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 24 (1) of the Act means a case where a radio station provided for in Article 24 (2) 1 undergoes an inspection under the main clause, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 24 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "completion inspection"). <Amended on Aug. 27, 2014; Dec. 27, 2022>

"In cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as where the outcomes of the sampling inspections of radio stations ... indicates a failure rate exceeding a certain threshold" in Article 24 (7) of the Act means where the failure rate exceeds 15/100 as a result of the sampling inspection conducted under paragraph (1).
Article 43 (Extension of deadline for completion of construction)
Article 43-2 (Deadline for re-inspection)
Article 44 (Effective period of regular inspections)

"Intervals prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the provisions, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 24 (4) of the Act means the period classified as follows: <Amended on Sep. 9, 2009; Jul. 26, 2010; Dec. 31, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Mar. 29, 2017; Jul. 26, 2017>
The following radio stations: One year:
A medical ship station (excluding medical ship stations referred to in subparagraph 2 (a) and (b));
A medical aircraft station (excluding medical aircraft stations referred to in subparagraph 2 (c));
An experimental station;
A development test station;
The following radio stations: Two years:
A medical ship station of a fishing boat, the gross tonnage of which is below 40 tons;
A medical ship station of a ship navigating only in the smooth water area defined in Article 2 (1) 3 (a) of the Enforcement Decree of the Ship Safety Act ;
A medical aircraft station of helicopters or light aircraft defined in subparagraph 1 or 26 of Article 2 of the Aviation Safety Act ;
Radio stations listed in Article 36 (1) 2-2 and 3: Three years;

Radio stations listed in Article 36 (1) 2: Five years; provided, it shall be two years for radio stations involved in life-saving or disasters, which are determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT.

If any of the following is applicable, the effective period of a regular inspection under paragraph (1) shall be counted from the relevant date: <Amended on Dec. 9, 2008; Dec. 31, 2010; Aug. 27, 2014; Jun. 30, 2016; Mar. 26, 2024>

Radio stations that have undergone the first regular inspection: Date an inspection certificate (hereinafter referred to as "certificate of inspection upon completion of construction") is issued under Article 24 (3) of the Act (referring to the date authorization for a radio station is obtained, in cases of radio stations listed in the subparagraphs of Article 24-2 (1) of the Act);

Radio stations that have undergone a subsequent regular inspection after the effective period of a regular inspection expires: Date following the day the effective period of the previous regular inspection expires;

Radio stations which have undergone an inspection under Article 24 (5) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "occasional inspection") during the effective period: Date a certificate of inspection is issued under Article 45 (7) (hereafter in this Article referred to as a "certificate of inspection") after undergoing an occasional inspection. In such cases, the effective period of the previous regular inspection shall be deemed expired on the day prior to the date a certificate of inspection is issued after undergoing the occasional inspection;

Radio stations that have undergone a regular inspection at the same time under Article 45 (2) 1 during the effective period of the regular inspection: Date following the expiration date of the effective period of the previous regular inspection of the radio station, whose effective period of the previous regular inspection expires first (hereafter in this subparagraph, referred to as "reference radio station"), among such radio stations. In this case, the effective period of the previous regular inspection of such radio stations shall be deemed to have expired on the expiration date of the effective period of the previous regular inspection of the reference radio station;

Radio stations that have undergone a regular inspection under article 45 (2) 2 or 3 again during the effective period of the regular inspection: Date a certificate of inspection is issued after undergoing the relevant regular inspection. In this case, the effective period of the previous regular inspection shall be deemed to have expired on the day prior to the date the certificate of inspection is issued.
Article 45 (Timing for and methods of inspections)

The time of a regular inspection under Article 24 (4) of the Act shall be classified as follows, and a radio station that has passed a regular inspection during the time shall be deemed to have undergone a regular inspection on the date the effective period of the regular inspection expires; provided, where it is impracticable to conduct a regular inspection during the time of the inspection classified under the following subparagraphs due to the occurrence of a disaster defined in the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety , the Minister of Science and ICT may separately determine the time of the regular inspection within the scope of one year from the expiry date of the time of the regular inspection: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Jan. 11, 2022>
A radio station referred to in Article 44 (1) 1: Within two months before or after the date the effective period of the regular inspection of the relevant radio station expires;

A radio station referred to in Article 44 (1) 2 and 3 and under the proviso of subparagraph 4 of that paragraph: Within three months before or after the date the effective period of the regular inspection of the relevant radio station expires;
A radio station referred to in Article 44 (1) 4: Within six months before or after the date the effective period of the regular inspection of the relevant radio station expires.

If any of the following is applicable, the Minister of Science and ICT may conduct a regular inspection of the radio station before the period for the relevant regular inspection prescribed in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1): <Amended on Mar. 26, 2024>

Where the Minister of Science and ICT deems it necessary to conduct regular inspections at the same time for the efficient management of radio waves and for the convenience of authorized persons, with regard to the radio stations that meet all of the following requirements:
The effective period of a regular inspection of each radio station shall be 5 years under the main clause of Article 44 (1) 4;

Two or more radio stations located at the same installation site or operated by the same authorized person (only applicable to radio stations with the same jurisdiction for inspection under the latter part of Article 42-2 (1));
Where the authorized person requests it;
Other cases where the Minister of Science and ICT deems it necessary to conduct a regular inspection before the period for the relevant regular inspection.

Regular inspections, occasional inspections, and inspections under Article 24 (8) of the Act shall be conducted according to the following classification, and matters necessary for inspections, such as detailed subject-matters of inspections, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Aug. 27, 2014; Dec. 3, 2014; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>

Performance inspections: Inspections of the performance of radio equipment, such as antenna power, radio frequencies, unwanted emissions, occupied bandwidth, equivalent isotopically radiated power, effective radiated power, and modulation factor;

Collated inspections: Inspections by collating and checking whether authorized persons, radio facilities, places of installation, posting of operators, etc. conform to the matters of authorization for or matters of reporting on radio stations, etc.

The head of an institution conducting regular inspections shall determine matters, such as the date of and fees for regular inspections, and notify the authorized persons of radio stations subject to inspection of such matters, no later than one month before the scheduled date for the regular inspection. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2016>

An occasional inspection may be conducted in any of the following cases; provided, the ratio of radio stations subject to an occasional inspection under subparagraph 1 shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, considering the failure rate within the range not exceeding a ratio computed by deducting the sampling ratio from 30/100: <Added on Aug. 27, 2014; Dec. 3, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 1, 2020>
Where the failure rate does not exceed 15/100 according to the result of a sampling inspection, the sampling ratio of which is less than 30/100;
Where the authorized person of a radio station requests an occasional inspection (limited to requests made to remove, or ascertain the effect of, interference);

Where the Minister of Science and ICT deems it particularly necessary for the efficient use or management of radio waves, such as where a ship or an aircraft fitted with a radio station intends to leave for a foreign country or where it is intended to prevent radio interference, etc. under Article 29 (2) of the Act.

The head of an institution conducting occasional inspections shall determine matters, such the date of and fees for occasional inspections, and notify in advance the authorized persons of radio stations subject to occasional inspections of such matters. <Added on Aug. 27, 2014; Jun. 30, 2016>

Where a person passes an inspection under Article 24 (4), (5) or (8) of the Act, a certificate of inspection shall be issued to him or her. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Aug. 27, 2014; Dec. 3, 2014; Jun. 30, 2016>

Circumstances in which it is necessary to conduct an inspection for the efficient use or management of radio waves under Article 24 (8) of the Act are as follows: <Amended on Dec. 3, 2014; Jun. 30, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 1, 2020>
Where it is necessary to ascertain whether the radio frequencies approved for use are actually being used;

Where the Minister of Science and ICT deems it particularly necessary for the efficient use or management of radio waves, such as where it is intended to prevent radio interference, etc. under Article 29 (2) of the Act.

A person conducting an inspection pursuant to Article 24 (1), (4), (5), and (8) of the Act shall present an identification indicating that he or she is a radio station inspector or a certificate of public official, to interested persons. <Amended on Dec. 3, 2014; Jun. 30, 2016>

Unless provided in this Decree, the time, methods of, and procedures for inspections under Article 24 (1), (4), (5), and (8) of the Act shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Added on Dec. 3, 2014; Jun. 30, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 45-2 (Exemption from completion inspections)
"Radio stations prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 24-2 (1) 1 of the Act means the following: <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 12, 2017; Jun. 23, 2020>
A ship station of a fishing boat fitted with radio facilities of less than 30 watts;
Any of the following amateur stations:
A radio station that uses radio equipment that has undergone a conformity assessment;

A radio station installed and operated by a person who has obtained an amateur radio operator license in a foreign country and is recommended by an organization designated by the Minister of Science and ICT during the period of his or her stay in the Republic of Korea of up to one month;
A radio station established for national security or Presidential security service;
A radio station established by the Government or a facility-based telecommunications business entity under the Telecommunications Business Act for emergency communications, not operated constantly;
A radio station established in high seas or polar regions;
A land mobile earth station established for operation in a foreign country;

A small-scale experimental station or development test station that meets the requirements determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT in relation to the area of use, purpose, etc.
"Radio stations prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 24-2 (1) 3 of the Act means the following: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>
Any of the following radio stations using radio equipment that have undergone a conformity assessment:
Portable radio equipment among radio facilities for mobile stations;
Portable radio equipment among radio facilities for land mobile stations;
Portable radio equipment among radio facilities for on-board communications stations;
Portable radio equipment for self-communications among radio facilities for trunked radio systems;
Automobile-mounted or portable radio equipment among radio facilities intended for the radiodetermination service;
A radio station which is a radio facility performing relay service only, and which changes the type of radio waves or receiving radio frequencies without changing a circuit;

A radio station, etc., determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, of which only antenna structure of radio facilities installed within a tunnel, basement of a building, etc. is changed.
Article 46 (Postponement of regular inspections)

A person who intends to postpone a regular inspection pursuant to Article 24-2 (2) of the Act shall file a written request to postpone the timing of regular inspections (including electronic documents) with the head of an inspection institution no later than the regular inspection date notified pursuant to Article 45 (4). <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Jun. 30, 2016>

Where the head of an inspection institution deems that the reasons for the postponement of a regular inspection under paragraph (1) are appropriate, he or she may approve postponement insofar as a postponement period ends before the date of the beginning of the regular inspection under Article 45 (1).
Article 47 (Exemption from regular inspection or omission thereof)
Radio stations under Article 24-2 (1) 5 of the Act;
Radio stations under Article 45-2 (1) 2 through 6 and under paragraph (2) of that Article.
Article 48 Deleted. <Dec. 31, 2010>
Article 49 (Exceptions to operation of radio stations)
Communications conducted for testing or adjusting radio equipment;

Communications between a coast station and a ship station, between ship stations, between an aeronautical station and an aircraft station, or between aircraft stations conducted for reference of meteorology or coordination of time;
Communications for medical calls (referring to notification on medical treatment of patients on board a ship or an aircraft while in navigation);

Communications concerning indication of the position of a ship or an aircraft (referring to indication of the position of a ship or an aircraft collected by domestic or foreign administrative agencies as required for rescue or search in cases of distress of a ship or an aircraft, which is transmitted and received by and between relevant administrative agencies, the relevant ship or aircraft);
Communications between a coast station and a ship station, between ship stations, between an aeronautical station and an aircraft station or between aircraft stations, in order to measure bearings;
Communications by a ship station to transmit a telegram for its authorized person's services to a coast station;
Communications by an aircraft station to transmit a telegram for its authorized person's services to an aeronautical station;

Communications transmitted by an aeronautical station to an aircraft station, communications concerning the navigational safety of an aircraft transmitted by an aeronautical station to another aeronautical station for delivery of urgent messages (only applicable where it is impracticable to attain the objective of relevant communications through other communication systems);
The following communications between aeronautical stations forming a communication network of aeronautical radiotelephony:
Notification transmitted by an aircraft station, which is a relay of communications to another aeronautical station within the relevant communications network;
Communications necessary for effective communication of communications within the relevant communications network;
The following communications between an aircraft station and a radio station in the maritime mobile service:
Communications processing the duties of supplying telecommunications services;
Communications concerning navigational safety of aircraft;
Communications necessary for cooperative work by ship and aircraft concerning rescue of distressed ship or distressed aircraft, etc.;

Urgent communications for authorized person's services between an aircraft station and a radio station in the maritime mobile service, land mobile service, or mobile service belong to the same authorized person;

Urgent communications for authorized person's duties between mobile stations belonging to the same authorized person and radio station in the maritime mobile service, aeronautical mobile service, or land mobile service belonging to such authorized person;

Communications concerning transportation of ships within a harbor, occurrence of maritime pollution, arrangement within a harbor, crackdown within a harbor or seaport quarantine conducted between a coast station of the State or a local government and a ship station or between ship stations;

Urgent communications for traffic arrangement, enforcement, quarantine and safety within an airport between aeronautical station of an air traffic control tower of the State or a local government and a land mobile station in motion within the relevant airport or between mobile stations;
Fishery communications or communications on the guidance and supervision of fisheries between a coast station and a ship station of a fishing boat or between ship stations of fishing boats;

Urgent communications concerning maritime security between a radio station in the maritime mobile service for maritime security or in the aeronautical mobile service and a ship station, aircraft station, or radio station in the radio-determination service;
Urgent communications concerning the maintenance of public order between radio stations of administrative agencies in charge of maintaining public order;
Communications for training to secure an emergency communications system.
Article 50 (Connection with, and use of, radio facilities)

The Minister of Science and ICT may grant authorization to an authorized person of a radio station who intends to connect his or her radio facilities with or to use the radio facilities of another authorized, if it is deemed specifically necessary to promote public welfare, such as emergency rescue. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
The Minister of Science and ICT shall give public notice upon granting authorization to connect to and use radio facilities pursuant to paragraph (1). <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 51 (Closure or suspension of operation)

A person who intends to report the closure, suspension, or re-operation of a radio station pursuant to Article 25-2 (1) of the Act shall file a report, stating the grounds therefor, with the Minister of Science and ICT or the Korea Communications Commission. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
The period for which a radio station can be suspended under paragraph (1) shall be at least one month but less than one year.
Article 52 (Notice to coast stations)

If any of the following is applicable, in accordance with Article 28 (3) of the Act, a ship station shall give notice to a coast station within the radius of communications in which the ship is located:
Where it enters into the radius of communications or intends to leave from the radius of communications;
Where it intends to close a radio station as it enters the port, or intends to establish a radio station as it leaves the port;
As for a ship station having no mandatory hours of operation, where it intends to close a radio station other than cases falling under subparagraph 2.
If any of the following is applicable, a ship station need not give notice to a coast station, notwithstanding paragraph (1):
Where it does not have the radio wave of a frequency received by a coast station within the radius of communications in which the ship locates;
Where it is a ship station operated by the Government or a public entity, and needs to keep the activities of the ship confidential in the conduct of business;
Where it is a ship station of a liner vessel and the ship enters or departs a port on schedule.
The radius of communications of a coast station referred to in paragraph (1) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 53 (Reporting on introduction or discard of radio wave blocking devices)
"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as financial resources and quantity" in Article 29 (4) of the Act means the following matters:
Specifications containing the name, type, and serial number of a radio wave blocking device under Article 29 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "radio wave blocking device");
Quantity of radio wave blocking devices to be introduced or discarded;
The date of introduction or discard of radio wave blocking devices.

The head of a central administrative agency required to report the introduction or discard of radio wave blocking devices (hereinafter referred to as "report on introduction or discard") pursuant to Article 29 (4) of the Act shall report the matters specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) to the Minister of Science and ICT within 15 days after the date of introduction or discard of the devices.
Article 53-2 (Authorization for manufacture, import, and sale of radio wave blocking devices)

A person who intends to obtain authorization for manufacture, import, or sale of radio wave blocking devices (hereinafter referred to as "authorization for manufacture, import, or sale") pursuant to Article 29 (5) of the Act shall submit to the Minister of Science and ICT an application for authorization for manufacture, import, or sale of radio wave blocking devices in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Science and ICT, accompanied by the documents stating the following matters:
Objectives for activities, measures, etc. falling under any subparagraph of Article 29 (3) of the Act;
The specifications and performance of the radio wave blocking devices to be manufactured, imported, or sold;
A block diagram of the radio wave blocking devices to be manufactured, imported, or sold;
The period required for manufacture, import, or sale.
A person who intends to obtain authorization for manufacture, import, or sale shall meet all of the following requirements:
The feasibility of the objectives referred to in paragraph (1) 1:
Appropriateness of radio frequencies emitted from the radio wave blocking device to be manufactured, imported, or sold.
Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT shall grant authorization only where all requirements under paragraph (2) are met.

When the Minister of Science and ICT grants authorization for manufacture, import, or sale, he or she shall determine the effective period of the authorization in consideration of the period prescribed in paragraph (1) 4.
Article 53-3 (Security measures following reporting or authorization related to radio wave blocking devices)
Article 53-4 (Criteria and procedures for compensation for losses)
The standards for compensation for losses incurred due to the use of radio waves blocking devices under Article 29-2 (2) of the Act shall be as specified in attached Appendix 5-2.

A person who intends to be compensated for a loss incurred due to the use of a radio wave blocking device pursuant to Article 29-2 (2) of the Act shall submit documents proving the details of the loss and the amount of the loss to the head of the central administrative agency (including its affiliated agencies; hereafter the same shall apply in this Article) or the head of an agency under its supervision using the radio wave blocking device.

Upon receipt of documents submitted under paragraph (2), the head of the central administrative agency or the head of the agency under its supervision using the spectrum blockade device shall calculate compensation in accordance with the standards for compensation for losses incurred due to the use of the radio wave blocking device specified in attached Appendix 5-2 within 90 days from the date of receipt of such documents; and shall pay the compensation to the person who has claimed the compensation for losses.
Article 54 (Filing applications for authorization to establish broadcasting stations)

A person who seeks to apply for authorization to establish a broadcasting station for the terrestrial broadcasting service pursuant to Article 34 (1) of the Act shall file an application for authorization (including an electronic application form) with the Korea Communications Commission along with a brief statement of facilities and construction drawings.

Where an application for authorization is filed to establish at least two terrestrial broadcasting auxiliary stations simultaneously (excluding terrestrial broadcasting auxiliary stations established underground or in a tunnel under Article 24 (3) 2), the applicant may submit only one application for authorization, a summary statement of facilities and construction drawings, irrespective of the number of radio stations, notwithstanding paragraph (1); provided,, where the place of installation, antenna type, antenna power, etc. for each radio station partially differ, he or she shall submit separate statements. <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016; Dec. 1, 2020>

Upon receipt of an application for authorization filed under paragraph (1) the Korea Communications Commission shall verify the corporate registration certificate (applicable only where the representative or executive of an existing radio station has been changed if the authorized person thereof seeks to obtain additional authorization to establish a radio station) by sharing the administrative information pursuant to Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act .
"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the latter part of Article 34 (4) of the Act means matters referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 31 (4).
Article 55 (Matters subject to examination in authorizing establishment of broadcasting stations)
Whether the incorporation is definite where the applicant is a corporation being incorporated;

Whether the applicant possesses broadcast studio facilities; provided, the same shall not apply where the applicant is to take exclusive charge of relaying broadcasting matters of another broadcasting station;
Whether the plans to install facilities for a broadcasting station are reasonable;
Whether the applicant has technical ability to operate a broadcasting station;

Whether antenna power does not exceed 50 kw in cases of a broadcasting station conducting a medium-wave broadcasting service; provided, the same shall not apply where the Minister of Science and ICT deems it especially necessary.
Article 56 (Conditions for establishing broadcasting stations conducting medium-frequency broadcasting service)

The place to install the transmitting antenna for a broadcasting station providing the medium-frequency broadcasting service shall meet the following conditions for establishment: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>

The number of households in the blanketing area of a broadcasting station to be established does not exceed 0.35 percent of the number of households in the broadcast service area of the broadcasting station;

The location of transmitting antenna for a broadcasting station to be established shall maintain a separation distance prescribed in the following table from any point of the place designated by the Minister of Science and ICT in consideration of population density, etc.; provided, where it is impracticable or unnecessary to maintain a separation distance due to geographical feature, the separation distance determined by the Minister of Science and ICT shall apply:

Where all or most part of the broadcast service area of a broadcasting station to be established overlaps with all or most part of the broadcast service area of another broadcasting station conducting a medium-wave broadcasting service, the transmitting antenna for the broadcasting station shall be installed in a place as near as possible to the place on which the transmitting antenna of another broadcasting station conducting a medium-wave broadcasting service is installed insofar as it does not adversely affect the reception of broadcast due to the electronic coupling of transmitting antennas with each other, etc.

The Minister of Science and ICT may relax conditions referred to in paragraph (1) where deemed specifically necessary to promote public welfare, etc. In such cases, he or she may order an authorized person to remove an obstruction to the reception of a relevant broadcast or to take other necessary measures. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 57 (Conditions for establishing ultra short-wave broadcasting stations or television broadcasting stations)

The transmitting antenna for a broadcasting station providing the ultra short-wave broadcasting service or television broadcasting service shall meet the following conditions for establishment: <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016>

That the place on which the transmitting antenna is to be installed shall be fit to generate efficient distribution of electric field strength in consideration of the population density of the area over which broadcasting is to be served, and that it shall be in a low position so that radio wave emission to areas other than the area over which broadcasting is to be served shall be suppressed to the maximum extent possible;

That the height, effective radiated power, and directivity of the transmitting antenna shall make the whole area of a major city enter the broadcast service area, and suppress unwanted emission to the maximum;
That it shall meet the conditions under Article 56 (1) 3.

Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a broadcasting station established by a community radio broadcasting business entity defined in subparagraph 3 (e) of Article 2 of the Broadcasting Act (hereinafter referred to as "community radio broadcasting station") among broadcasting stations providing the ultra short-wave broadcasting service shall meet the following conditions for establishment: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 18, 2018>
That its antenna power shall not exceed 10 watts;
That it shall have an output control device that cannot exceed the authorized antenna power. In such cases, the output control device shall be sealed in a way so that breaking the seal is difficult;
That height and directivity of a transmitting antenna shall not exceed its broadcast service area;
That it shall meet the technical requirements determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, such as the bandwidth, and height of antenna.

The Minister of Science and ICT may relax the conditions provided for in paragraphs (1) and (2) where deemed specifically necessary to promote public welfare, etc. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 58 (Broadcast service area)

The broadcast service area of each broadcasting station (excluding satellite broadcasting stations; hereafter the same shall apply in this Article) shall be marked on a map according to the classification of the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan Cities, Do s, Special Self-Governing Province, Si s, Gun s, Gu s (referring to autonomous Gu s), etc., and matters regarding the anticipated listenership for a broadcasting service, such as the total number of households, number of households anticipated to listen to the broadcasting, etc. in the range.

Detailed methods of marking the broadcast service area under paragraph (1) and guidelines for preparation shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

A person who is authorized to establish a broadcasting station shall submit data on the actual measurement of electric field strength of the broadcast service area to the Minister of Science and ICT within three months from the time the broadcasting station begins operations. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 59 (Protection of broadcasting reception)

Every owner of a building (hereinafter referred to as "owner") causing interference with broadcast (applicable only to television broadcasting) reception (hereinafter referred to as "interference with reception") shall install facilities necessary to remove such interference with reception and maintain the facilities pursuant to Article 36 (1) of the Act.

The standards for ordinarily receivable broadcast and the level of removal of interference with reception under Article 36 (1) of the Act shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 60 (Occurrence and mediation of disputes)

Any resident of an area experiencing interference with reception (hereinafter referred to as "resident") may report the occurrence of interference with reception to the head of the agency that has permitted the construction of the relevant building.
Upon receipt of a report under paragraph (1), the head of the agency that has permitted the construction of the relevant building shall notify the relevant owner of such fact.

Where no agreement is reached between the owner and residents concerning removal of interference with reception, the residents may apply for mediation to the head of the agency that has permitted the construction of the relevant building.

The head of the agency that has permitted the construction of the relevant building shall take appropriate measures to settle the dispute, and may request cooperation from the Minister of Science and ICT, where necessary. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 61 (Measures taken by authorized persons of broadcasting stations)

Where an owner intends to remove interference with reception caused by radio facilities determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, the authorized person of the broadcasting station, which is experiencing interference with reception, shall take necessary measures, such as applying for authorization for a radio station to remove such interference with reception. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
The authorized person of a broadcasting station may require an owner to bear expenses, etc. incurred in establishing a radio station under paragraph (1).
Article 62 (Investigation of interference)
Investigation of the details and scope of the occurrence of interference with reception;
Measures to remove interference with reception;
Grading standards for the reception of ordinarily receivable broadcasts in the relevant area.
Article 63 (Filing applications for international registration of satellite networks)

A person who intends to apply for international registration of a satellite network pursuant to Article 39 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "applicant") shall file an application accompanied by the following documents with the Minister of Science and ICT: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Documents specified by the Radio Regulations of the International Telecommunication Union;
A satellite project plan.

Where the Minister of Science and ICT deems that the contents of an application filed under paragraph (1) comply with the following requirements, he or she shall file an application for international registration of a satellite network with the International Telecommunication Union: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
That it shall be possible to assign and designate a radio frequency to the satellite station that the applicant intends to establish;
That the satellite project plan shall be appropriate;
That the applicant shall have the capability to adjust interference with satellite networks.

Where the contents of an application do not comply with any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (2), the Minister of Science and ICT may require the relevant applicant to supplement them within a specified period. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

If deemed necessary to address interference with a satellite network, the Minister of Science and ICT may require an applicant to adjust satellite network interference under the jurisdiction of a foreign country. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 64 (Fees for international registration of satellite networks)
Fees for international registration of a satellite network under Article 39 (3) of the Act shall be as specified by the International Telecommunication Union.

The Minister of Science and ICT may select satellite networks exempt from fees for international registration of satellite networks each year, as specified by the International Telecommunication Union. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 64-2 (Periods of restrictions on transfer or lease of satellite frequency license)

"Such period as provided by Presidential Decree" in the main clause of Article 41 (2) of the Act means the three-year period beginning on the date of assignment or designation of a satellite radio frequency, etc. under Article 10 (2) of the Act or Article 18-4 of the Act.
"Cause prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 41 (2) of the Act means cases classified as follows:
Transfer of a satellite frequency license:
When a person, who is assigned a satellite radio frequency, etc. or obtains designation, becomes insolvent;

When a person, who is assigned a satellite radio frequency, etc. or obtains designation, merges with another entity, or transfers all of the business that he or she operates to another entity to cope with sudden changes in economic conditions or to streamline his or her business;
Leasing of a satellite frequency license: When a person obtains re-assignment under Article 16 of the Act;

Discontinuation of the use of a satellite radio frequency, etc.: When a satellite radio frequency, etc. cannot be used in the normal conditions due to serious fault or failure of all or part of a satellite.
Article 64-3 (Approval to transfer or lease satellite frequency licenses)

A person who intends to acquire or take on lease a satellite frequency license under the main clause of, or proviso of, Article 41 (2) of the Act shall file an application for approval in the Form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Science and ICT, accompanied by the following documents (including electronic documents), with the Minister of Science and ICT, together with a person who intends to transfer or lease out the satellite frequency license pursuant to paragraph (3) of that Article: <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>
A copy of a transfer/acquisition contract (only applicable to transfer and acquisition) or a copy of a lease/hire contract (only applicable to lease and hire);
The articles of incorporation of the relevant corporation;
A list of stockholders of the relevant corporation, and documents regarding the ownership of stocks, etc. of stockholders, etc.;
Plans for using satellite radio frequencies;
Measures for protecting satellite networks and users;
Documents determined by the public announcement of radio frequency assignment pursuant to the latter part of Article 10 (21) of the Act and Article 11 of this Decree.

A person who intends to transfer or lease out a satellite frequency license under the proviso of Article 41 (2) of the Act shall also submit the documents classified as follows, in addition to the documents referred to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1):
In cases of transfer: Documents proving the fact falling under any item of Article 64-2 (2) 1;
In cases of lease: Documents proving the fact falling under Article 64-2 (2) 2.

Upon receipt of an application for approval filed under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT shall verify the relevant corporate registration certificate by sharing the administrative information pursuant to Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act . <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>

Upon receipt of an application for approval filed under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT shall determine whether to grant approval taking into account the following matters, within 30 days of receipt of the application, and inform the applicant of his or her determination: <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>
Impacts on the protection of satellite networks;
Efficient use of spectrum resources;
The applicant’s financial capacity;
The applicant’s technological capacity;
Characteristics of the radio frequency to be assigned or other matters necessary for using the radio frequency.
Article 64-4 (Approval for interruption of use of satellite radio frequencies)

A person who intends to interrupt the use of satellite radio frequencies, etc. under the main clause of, or proviso of, Article 41 (2) of the Act shall file an application for approval in the Form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Science and ICT, accompanied by documents describing measures for protecting satellite networks and users (including electronic documents), with the Minister of Science and ICT pursuant to paragraph (3) of that Article. <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>

Any person who intends to interrupt the use of satellite radio frequencies, etc. under the proviso of Article 41 (2) of the Act shall also submit documents proving the fact falling under Article 64-2 (2) 3, in addition to the documents referred to in paragraph (1).

Upon receipt of an application for approval filed under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT shall verify the relevant corporate registration certificate by sharing the administrative information pursuant to Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act . <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>

Upon receipt of an application for approval filed under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT shall determine whether to grant approval taking into account the following matters, within 30 days of receipt of the application, and inform the applicant of his or her determination: <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>
Impacts on the protection of satellite networks;
Impacts on the protection of users.
Article 64-5 (Transfer or lease of radio facilities of space stations)

An authorized person, etc., of a space station who intends to transfer or lease out the whole or part of the radio facilities of a space station to another person (including the operation of such radio facilities by entrustment to other person or use thereof jointly with another person) pursuant to Article 42-2 (1) of the Act shall file an application for approval in the Form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Science and ICT, accompanied by following documents (including electronic documents), with the Minister of Science and ICT together with a person who intends to acquire or take on lease the relevant radio facilities: <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>

A copy of a transfer/acquisition contract (only applicable to transfer and acquisition), a copy of a lease/hire contract (only applicable to lease and hire), a copy of an agreement on entrusted operation (only applicable to entrusted operation) or a contract on joint use (only applicable to joint use);
The articles of incorporation of the relevant corporation;
A list of stockholders of the relevant corporation, and documents regarding the ownership of stocks, etc. of stockholders, etc.;
A satellite project plan.

Upon receipt of an application for approval filed under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT shall verify the relevant corporate registration certificate by sharing the administrative data information pursuant to Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act . <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>

Upon receipt of an application for approval filed under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT shall determine whether to grant approval taking into account the following matters, within 30 days of receipt of the application, and inform the applicant of his or her determination: <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>
Efficient use of the radio facilities of the space station;
Maintenance of order of using satellite radio waves;
Impacts on the protection of satellite networks.
Article 64-6 (Submission of plans for operating satellites)

In accordance with Article 44-2 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT may request a person who is operating a satellite in any satellite network, the international registration of which is completed by the Republic of Korea, to submit a plan to secure and operate a subsequent satellite (hereinafter referred to as a "plan for satellite operation") by five years prior to the expiration of the expected service life (referring to the expected service life stated in the plan to use radio frequencies referred to in Article 12 (1) 　 3 and the satellite project plan referred to in Article 63 (1) 2) of the relevant satellite. <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>
The plan for satellite operation shall include the following matters:
The satellite orbits and radio frequencies of the subsequent satellite;
The production schedule, and the date scheduled for launch of the subsequent satellite;
The expected service life of the subsequent satellites;
The satellite project plan.
Article 65 (Radio stations subject to reporting on electromagnetic field strength)
Article 66 (Timing for and methods of reporting electromagnetic field strength)

The timing for reporting the electromagnetic field strength under Article 47-2 (3) of the Act is classified as follows; provided, only subparagraph 1 shall apply to radio stations of electromagnetic grade I, which shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT under Article 47-2 (1) 2 of the Act: <Amended on Dec. 9, 2008; Dec. 31, 2010; Aug. 27, 2014; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 12, 2017; Dec. 1, 2020; Jan. 11, 2022>

A radio station required to undergo an inspection upon completion of construction under Article 24 (1) of the Act [applicable only to changed matters under Article 31 (4) 3, 6, 7, and 9, and Article 39-2 (3) 1 (applicable only to matters regarding the antenna power, and the type and configuration of the antenna, and antenna gain; provided, cases where a change results in a drop of electromagnetic field strength shall be excluded herefrom), 2, and 4]: Within 45 days from the date of receipt of a certificate of the completion inspection; provided, a radio station having a transmitter with more than 500 watt antenna power (if at least two transmitters share the same radio frequency, the antenna power of each transmitter shall be aggregated; hereinafter the same shall apply) shall report it on the date of receipt of a certificate of the completion inspection;

A radio station required to undergo a regular inspection under Article 24 (4) of the Act: Within 45 days from the date of receipt of a certificate of a regular inspection after passing an inspection under Article 24 (4) of the Act.

Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the timing for reporting on the electromagnetic field strength under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) may be extended in unavoidable circumstances, such as the spread of infectious diseases under the Infectious Disease Control and Prevention Act . <Added on Dec. 1, 2020>

An authorized person who intends to extend the timing for reporting on the electromagnetic field strength pursuant to paragraph (2) shall apply for the extension of the timing for reporting to the Minister of Science and ICT in writing specifying the grounds for and the period of extension before the timing for reporting expires under paragraph (1). <Added on Dec. 1, 2020>
Where the Minister of Science and ICT deems the grounds for the application filed under paragraph (3) reasonable, the Minister may approve the extension. <Added on Dec. 1, 2020>

In calculating the timing for reporting on the electromagnetic field strength under paragraph (1) (including the timing for reporting whose extension is approved under paragraph (4)), holidays and Saturdays shall not be included. <Added on Dec. 1, 2020>
Article 67 (Timing for and methods of requesting measurement of electromagnetic field strength)
A radio station required to undergo an inspection upon completion of construction under Article 24 (1) of the Act: Date a report on completion of construction is submitted under Article 42 ;
A radio station required to undergo a regular inspection under Article 24 (4) of the Act: Within 30 days from the date a notice of a regular inspection is served under Article 45 (4).
Article 67-2 (Technical requirements for electromagnetic compatibility)

The technical requirements for electromagnetic compatibility referred to in Article 47-3 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "technical requirements for electromagnetic compatibility") are as follows:

Equipment causing electromagnetic interference shall be managed to protect a broadcasting and communications network in accordance with the following criteria and not to hinder the performance of other equipment:
The electromagnetic energy from the voltage or current flowing through a power cable or signal cable shall not adversely affect other communications networks, peripheral devices, etc.;
Electric field strength or electromagnetic energy of electricity, etc. radiating into the air shall not adversely affect other communications networks, peripheral devices, etc.;

Equipment affected by electromagnetic waves shall be managed so that malfunction or performance degradation shall not occur in an environment in which electromagnetic waves exist according to the following criteria:
Malfunction or performance degradation shall not occur due to electromagnetic energy existing in the air or due to electromagnetic energy from power cable, signal cable, etc.;
Malfunction or performance degradation shall not occur under the influence of instantaneous changes in electromagnetic wave energy, such as static electricity of changes in rated voltage, etc.

Detailed technical requirements for electromagnetic compatibility referred to in paragraph (1) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 68 (Lease of radio facilities)

An authorized person who intends to lease out radio facilities at a radio station (excluding radio facilities of a space station) to a third person pursuant to Article 48 (1) of the Act shall file an application for approval to lease radio facilities with the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>

Where the Minister of Science and ICT deems that an application filed under paragraph (1) is appropriate for using radio facilities efficiently and for maintaining sound practices in the use of radio waves, he or she shall grant approval for lease. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Where the Minister of Science and ICT grants approval for lease pursuant to paragraph (2), he or she may limit the period of lease and area of use, if particularly necessary. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 69 (Entrusted operation and joint use of radio facilities)

Radio facilities (excluding radio facilities of a space station) that can be operated under entrustment or be jointly used pursuant to Article 48 (1) of the Act are listed as follows: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>
Antenna poles at radio stations;
Transmitting facilities and receiving facilities.
Radio facilities at radio stations belonging to the same authorized person;
Radio facilities at amateur stations determined by the Minister of Science and ICT;
Other radio facilities at radio stations for public safety, which are deemed particularly necessary and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT.
Where radio facilities referred to in paragraph (1) are operated under entrustment or are jointly used, the following conditions shall be met: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
The radio facilities shall be installed at a place where radio waves can be efficiently emitted;
The operation of pre-existing radio stations shall not be hindered;
Radio waves emitted from the radio facilities shall not interfere with the reception of broadcast signals by the neighborhood;
The radio facilities shall satisfy the criteria determined by the Minister of Science and ICT as deemed necessary.

A person who intends to obtain approval from the Minister of Science and ICT to entrust the operation of or jointly use radio facilities under paragraph (1) shall prepare an agreement or a contract for joint use and file an application for approval for entrusted operation or joint use of radio facilities with the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 69-2 (Orders to jointly use radio facilities)

The following are prescribed as the conditions for issuing an order to jointly use radio facilities and an order to install radio facilities in an environmentally friendly manner pursuant to Article 48-2 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "order for joint use, etc."):
Radio facilities installed and operated in the national or public park areas, development restriction districts, etc., which are deemed likely to damage the natural environment;
Radio facilities installed in urban areas, which are deemed likely to their fine view;
Radio facilities installed and operated in buildings, on roads, empty building sites, etc., which are deemed likely to damage the urban view or the natural environment.

Radio facilities subject to an order for joint use, etc. shall be the following radio facilities installed in base stations, mobile relay stations, and fixed stations established and operated by a facility-based telecommunications business entity: <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016; Jun. 23, 2020>
Antenna poles at radio stations;
Transmitting facilities and receiving facilities.
The Minister of Science and ICT shall take into account the following matters when issuing an order for joint use: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Whether radio wave interference is likely to occur;
Whether a building or land can be rented;
Whether buildings, rooftops, steel towers, etc. are safe;
Whether the electromagnetic field strength exceeds the technical requirements for human exposure to electromagnetic wave (applicable only to orders for joint use of radio facilities);
Whether it is possible to install radio facilities underground or in a tunnel or building (applicable only to orders for environmentally friendly installation of radio facilities);
Other matters deemed necessary by the Minister of Science and ICT for the efficient operation, management, etc. of radio facilities.
The Minister of Science and ICT shall give written notice, stating the following matters to issue an order for joint use, etc.: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Name of the radio station to be used jointly or environmentally friendly;
Place of installation of radio facilities;
Duration of installation of radio facilities;

Details necessary for the requirements, procedures, etc. for an order for joint use, etc. and for radio facilities to be issued an order for joint use, etc. under paragraphs (1) through (4) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 70 (Spectrum monitoring)
Detection of unwanted emission from home appliances, factory automation facilities, etc.;

Monitoring of and measures against communications causing interference or jamming, unwanted communications and false communications that incur inconvenience to radio communications;
Mobile spectrum monitoring;
Other matters regarding data surveys, measures and publicity necessary for maintaining and protecting the orderly use of radio waves.
Article 71 (Buildings requiring approval)

The following are prescribed as buildings or structures (hereinafter referred to as "building, etc.") requiring approval from the Minister of Science and ICT pursuant to Article 52 (1) of the Act: <Amended on Jun. 20, 2008; Nov. 2, 2009; Dec. 31, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017; Jan. 5, 2021>
The following buildings, etc. to be constructed in an area within one-kilometer radius from the place where the radio direction finder is installed:
Transmitting antennas and receiving antennas; provided, small-sized antennas for receiving broadcast and those equivalent thereto shall be excluded;
Overhead lines and elevated cables (including those for electricity, communications, electric railroads, and others equivalent thereto);

Buildings (including those made from wood, stone, and concrete and those of other structures); provided, where the angle of elevation of the top of a building, etc. from where the radio direction finder is installed does not exceed three degrees, such buildings shall be excluded;

Tower poles made from steel, stone, or wood and their supports, chimneys, and lightning arrestors; provided, where the angle of elevation of the top of a tower pole from the place where the radio direction finder is installed does not exceed three degrees, such tower pole shall be excluded;
Railroads and trolleys;

Water pipes, gas pipes, electric cables, communication cables buried in an area within 500-meter radius from the place where the radio direction finder is installed and other underground utilities equivalent thereto.

A person who intends to construct any of the buildings, etc. referred to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) shall file an application for approval to construct a building, etc. along with an elevation drawing and floor plan describing the external appearance of high floors (scale, bearing, height, and width shall be stated) with the Minister of Science and ICT. The same shall apply to filing an application for revising approved matters. <Amended on Jun. 20, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Where an application for approval under paragraph (2) is filed, the Minister of Science and ICT may request necessary materials from the applicant within a specified period, if necessary for determining whether electromagnetic interference exists. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Upon receipt of an application for approval or for approval of revision under paragraph (2), the Minister of Science and ICT shall examine whether electromagnetic interference exists and notify the applicant of his or her decision within 14 days. <Amended on Jun. 20, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
