Article 74 (Industrial, scientific, and medical equipment not deemed communications equipment)

Industrial equipment (referring to those used for industrial production, such as drying wood or plywood, melting or heating metals, exhaust of vacuum tubes, etc. after generating high-frequency energy);
Medical equipment (referring to those generating high-frequency energy to use such energy for medical purposes);

Other industrial, scientific, and medical equipment (other than those provided in subparagraphs 1 and 2, which use high-frequency energy for the purpose of heating, ionization, etc. by directly supplying high-frequency energy).
Article 75 (Industrial, scientific, and medical equipment deemed communications equipment)

"Facilities and equipment, the electric field strength, etc. of which satisfies the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 58 (1) 2 of the Act means any of the following equipment: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Communication equipment using power lines (hereinafter referred to as "power-line communication equipment") shall have electric field strength exceeding 500 microvolts (μV/m) at a three-meter radius from the equipment; provided, where the frequency of the relevant equipment is lower than 450 KHz, the equipment shall be the one exceeding the electric field strength publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT;

Inductive radiotelegraphy or radiotelephone (hereinafter referred to as "inductive communications equipment") shall have electric field strength exceeding 15 microvolts per meter at 500 meters away from the equipment and at a distance computed by dividing the basic frequency from cable by two π.
Frequencies emitted from power-line communication equipment and output to be used shall meet the following: <Amended on Jun. 20, 2008>
9 KHz and 30 MHz frequency range (excluding on-the-spot experiments for technical development);
The high frequency power of transmitting facilities shall not exceed 10 watts; provided, those of special equipment shall be excluded.
Frequencies emitted from inductive communication equipment shall be between 9 KHz and 250 KHz.
Article 76 (Authorization for industrial, scientific and medical equipment)

A person who intends to obtain authorization for industrial, scientific, and medical equipment pursuant to Article 58 (1) of the Act shall file an application for authorization with the Minister of Science and ICT, along with a construction drawing of the industrial, scientific and medical equipment, as classified below: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Equipment referred to in Article 74 : To file an application for each place where the relevant equipment is to be installed;
Equipment referred to in Article 75 (1): To file an application for each communication system to which the relevant equipment pertains.

Where a person who intends to apply for authorization pursuant to paragraph (1) intends to use all of the industrial, scientific, and medical equipment, which has been used by a third person upon obtaining authorization, unceasingly as they stand, the following documents may replace construction drawings of the industrial, scientific and medical equipment:
A copy of a certificate of authorization for the equipment for which authorization is current;
A map showing a new place of installation and its environs, where equipment is to be newly installed in a place different from the current place of installation;
Documents indicating the transfer of ownership, etc.

The Minister of Science and ICT shall issue to the applicant, a certificate of authorization for industrial, scientific, and medical equipment upon granting authorization for industrial, scientific, and medical equipment. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the latter part, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 58 (1) of the Act means the following: <Added on Dec. 31, 2010; Dec. 3, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
Purpose of operations;
Place of installation;

Type, name, and serial number of equipment; provided, industrial, scientific, and medical equipment determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT taking into account the degree, method, etc. of shielding electromagnetic waves shall be excluded;
Type of radio waves and frequency;
High frequency power.
Article 77 (Inspections of industrial, scientific, and medical equipment)

Inspections of industrial, scientific, and medical equipment under Article 58 (3) of the Act shall be conducted on each radio transmitter; provided, the facilities and equipment referred to in the proviso of Article 58 (3) of the Act may undergo an inspection on all radio transmitters using the same frequency at once. <Added on Dec. 27, 2022>
The regular inspection of industrial, scientific, and medical equipment conducted under Article 58 (3) of the Act shall be valid for five years. <Amended on Dec. 27, 2022>

Article 44 (2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the starting point for counting the term of validity of an inspection of industrial, scientific, and medical equipment; Article 45 (1) 3, and (5) 2 and 3 to the time of inspection; Article 45 (3), (4), (6), (7), (9), and (10) to the methods, procedures, etc. for inspections; and Article 46 to the postponement of regular inspections, respectively. <Amended on Aug. 27, 2014; Dec. 3, 2014; Jun. 30, 2016; Dec. 27, 2022>

"Multilateral-shielding facility prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 58 (3) of the Act means a facility with a shielding facility covering the industrial, scientific, and medical equipment within any of the following buildings: <Newly Inserted on Dec. 27, 2022; Dec. 17, 2024>
A building made of reinforced concrete without windows;
Any other building constructed to shield electromagnetic waves at a level equivalent to that of a building specified in subparagraph 1.
Article 77-2 (Certification of conformity)

The following are prescribed as broadcasting and communications equipment that requires certification of conformity under Article 58-2 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "certification of conformity"), and equipment that causes electromagnetic interference or are affected by electromagnetic waves (hereinafter referred to as "broadcasting and communications equipment, etc."):
Broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. likely to harm the spectrum environment, broadcasting and communications networks, etc.;
Broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. that causes significant electromagnetic interference or are affected by electromagnetic waves to the extent that it does not function normally;
Other broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. likely to inflict grave harm on the life and safety of people, etc.

A person who intends to obtain certification of conformity shall file an application for certification of conformity (including an electronic application form) accompanied by the documents publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, such as a component layout, and exterior drawings, with the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Where the Minister of Science and ICT grants certification of conformity to an application under paragraph (2), he or she shall issue a certificate to the applicant and publicly announce such fact in the Official Gazette. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Detailed matters necessary for the subject, procedures, methods, etc. of certification of conformity under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 77-3 (Registration of conformity and self-declaration of conformity)

Article 77-2 (2) through (4) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures and methods for and public announcement of registration of conformity under Article 58-2 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "registration of conformity").

"Equipment prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as equipment which is less likely to cause harm to the spectrum environment, broadcasting and communications networks, etc." in Article 58-2 (4) of the Act means any of the following equipment determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017; Jul. 26, 2017; Jul. 23, 2024>
Broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. used for measurement and testing;
Broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. used for industrial and scientific purposes;
Broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. which are less likely to harm the spectrum environment, broadcasting and communications networks, etc.;
Other broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. not requiring testing by designated testing bodies, in view of its characteristics, use, etc.
"Organization capable of testing as prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 58-2 (4) of the Act means any the following testing bodies: <Added on Jul. 23, 2024>
Testing bodies under mutual recognition agreements under Article 58-8 (5) of the Act;

Testing bodies recognized by domestic and foreign accreditation bodies that have entered into mutual recognition agreements on conformity assessment with International Accreditation Forum under Article 25 (1) of the Framework Act on National Standards .

A person that intends to manage in writing and disclose the fact that the relevant equipment meets the technical requirements for conformity assessment pursuant to Article 58-2 (4) of the Act shall manage the following matters in writing and disclose them on the website determined by the Minister of Science and ICT. Detailed matters necessary for the management in writing and disclosure in such cases shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT: <Added on Jul. 23, 2024>
The person's trade name or name;
The name and model name of the equipment;
The identification number of the equipment;
The manufacturer and manufacturing country of the equipment;
Appearance photos of the equipment;
The technical requirements for conformity assessment under Article 58-2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "technical requirements for conformity assessment") applied to the equipment;
Other matters determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT.

Each of the following persons shall retain documents determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, such as test documents on the technical requirements for conformity assessment, until 5 years after the cessation of manufacture, import, or sale from the date classified as follows, pursuant to Article 58-2 (5) of the Act: <Amended on Jul. 23, 2024; Apr. 1, 2025>
A person that has filed for registration of conformity: The date on which the person has filed for the registration of conformity;

A person that has made a self-conformity declaration under Article 58-2 (4) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "self-conformity declaration"): The date on which the person has made the self-conformity declaration;
A person that modifies any of the facts in the person's declaration of self-conformity: The date on which the person modifies any of the facts in the person's declaration of self-conformity.
Article 77-4 (Reporting on modification regarding conformity assessment)

Where any modification is made to the matters that have undergone conformity assessment under the former part of Article 58-2 (6) of the Act, the person shall submit a report on modification regarding conformity assessment (including an electronic report form) to the Minister of Science and ICT, along with documents proving the fact of modification (including electronic documents). In this regard, where such modification is made to the matters related to the technical requirements for conformity assessment, such report shall be filed after conformity assessment is conducted. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017; Jul. 23, 2024>

Where a person that has made a self-conformity declaration intends to modify any of the facts in the self-conformity declaration pursuant to Article 58-2 (7) of the Act, the person shall manage in writing the matters to be modified among the matters referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 77-3 (4) and disclose them on the website determined by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Added on Jul. 23, 2024>

Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), detailed matters necessary for reporting on modification regarding conformity assessment and modification, etc. of facts in self-conformity declarations shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Added on Jul. 23, 2024>
Article 77-5 (Indication of conformity assessment)

A person that intends to indicate a conformity assessment mark under the former part of Article 58-2 (8) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "conformity assessment mark") shall indicate the following matters; provided, a person that has made a self-conformity declaration may indicate only the matters referred to in subparagraphs 5 and 6: <Amended on Jul. 23, 2024>
The trade name or name of the person that has undergone conformity assessment;
The name of the equipment;
The date of manufacturing of the equipment;
The manufacturer and manufacturing country of the equipment;
An integrated national certification mark under Article 22-4 of the Framework Act on National Standards ;
The model name and identification number of the equipment.

A person who intends to indicate the self-conformity declaration mark under the latter part of Article 58-2 (8) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "self-conformity declaration mark") in the product guide, etc. of equipment shall indicate the address of the website under Article 77-3 (4) and the matters under paragraph (1) 1 through 4. <Added on Jul. 23, 2024>

Matters necessary for the technical requirements and methods for indicating conformity assessment marks and self-conformity declaration marks shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017; Jul. 23, 2024>
Article 77-6 (Interim certification)

Article 77-2 (2) through (4) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures, methods, and public announcement, etc. of interim certification under Article 58-2 (9) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "interim certification"). <Amended on Jul. 23, 2024>

The Minister of Science and ICT may organize and operate an interim certification examination committee, as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, if deemed necessary to examine an application for interim certification under paragraph (1). <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

A person who applies for interim certification or has obtained interim certification pursuant to paragraph (1) may request the Minister of Science and ICT to establish or amend technical requirements for conformity assessment, if necessary to perform his or her business affairs. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Where a person who has obtained interim certification intends to undergo conformity assessment pursuant to Article 58-2 (10) of the Act, the person shall undergo conformity assessment under Article 58-2 (2) through (4) of the Act by no later than 90 days from the date on which the person is notified of the establishment of the technical requirements for conformity assessment applicable to the relevant equipment or becomes aware that any cause making it impracticable to conduct conformity assessment no longer exists. <Added on Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 23, 2024>
Article 77-7 (Exemption from conformity assessment)
The equipment which may be exempted from conformity assessment under Article 58-3 (1) of the Act shall be as stated in Appendix 6-2. <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016>
Article 77-2 (2) through (4) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures and methods for exemption from conformity assessment under paragraph (1) and other relevant matters.
Article 77-8 (Revocation of conformity assessment)

The Minister of Science and ICT shall give public announcement in the Official Gazette upon revoking conformity assessment pursuant to Article 58-4 (1) or (2) of the Act. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
"Period prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 58-4 (2) 1 of the Act means a period classified as follows:
Where disposition of revocation is issued for any of the reasons provided for in Article 58-4 (1) or 58-4 (2) 2 of the Act: Six months;
Where disposition of revocation is issued for the reason provided for in Article 58-4 (2) 1 of the Act: One year.
Article 77-9 (Designation of testing bodies)

A corporation intending to be designated as a testing body performing testing affairs for conformity assessment pursuant to Article 58-5 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "testing body") shall file an application (including an electronic application form) for designation of a testing body with the Minister of Science and ICT, along with documents determined by the Minister of Science and ICT, according to the following classification: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Aug. 27, 2014; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>
Wired field;
Wireless field;
Electromagnetic compatibility field;
Electromagnetic field strength field;
Specific absorption rate field.

The Minister of Science and ICT may require a specialized examination organization referred to in Article 77-10 to conduct the examination of requirements if deemed necessary for examining an application for designation filed under paragraph (1). <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>

Where the Minister of Science and ICT designates a testing body based on an application filed under paragraph (1), he or she shall issue a certificate of designation and publicly announce such fact in the Official Gazette and the website of the Ministry. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017; Jul. 23, 2024>

Detailed matters necessary for the procedures and methods for, and examination of applications for designation under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Where a testing body designated under paragraph (3) (hereinafter referred to as "designated testing body") intends to obtain approval for revising any terms and conditions of such designation, for abolishing designated testing duties, or for succession to the status pursuant to Article 58-5 of the Act, paragraphs (2) through (4) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures and methods for, public announcement thereof.
Article 77-10 (Specialized examination institutions)

"Specialized examination institution prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 58-5 (4) of the Act means an institution designated and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT from among institutions meeting the requirements for examination of designated testing bodies established by the International Organization for Standardization. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

The specialized examination institutions designated under paragraph (1) shall perform the duties of examination, as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 77-11 (Inspections of designated testing bodies)
Inspections of designated testing bodies prescribed in Article 58-6 of the Act shall be classified into regular inspections and occasional inspections. <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016>
The regular inspections referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with the following classifications: <Added on Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 23, 2024>

To inspect the performance of facilities necessary for conformity assessment testing (limited to facilities specified in subparagraphs 1 through 5 and 13 of Appendix 14-2) referred to in Article 58-5 (1) 1 of the Act: To be conducted at intervals determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, taking into account the frequency of use, durability, etc. of the relevant facilities;
To inspect matters other than those prescribed in subparagraph 1: To be conducted every two years, starting from the date of designation as a designated testing body.
The occasional inspections referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted at any time when inspections are required. <Added on Jun. 21, 2016>

To request relevant data pursuant to Article 58-6 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT shall make a written request (including electronic documents) specifying a 15-day period for submission; provided, where a person requested to provide reasonable grounds, he or she may extend the deadline for submission by up to 15 days. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 21, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>

Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (4), detailed procedures for inspecting designated testing bodies and other necessary matters shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Added on Jul. 23, 2024>
Article 77-12 (Matters to be observed by designated testing bodies)
Designated testing bodies shall abide by the following pursuant to Article 58-7 (1) of the Act: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 3, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
To appropriately maintain and manage examination-related facilities;
To regularly educate examination-related personnel;
To keep and maintain examination-related data for at least five years;

To conduct the sampling inspection of equipment equivalent to 3/100 of broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. the conformity of which are registered after undergoing tests conducted by a designated testing body under Article 58-2 (3) of the Act and report the results to the Minister of Science and ICT;
To establish and implement provisions governing examination-related quality management set by the International Organization for Standardization.

Where the Minister of Science and ICT issues a suspension order or imposes a revocation under paragraph (1), he or she shall publicly announce such fact in the Official Gazette and the website of the Ministry. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017; Jul. 23, 2024>

Matters to be observed and public announcements under paragraphs (1) and (2), and other necessary matters, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 77-13 (Mutual recognition agreements on conformity assessment)
Matters regarding the validity of conformity assessment;
Matters regarding technical requirements for conformity assessment;
Matters regarding testing bodies and certification bodies for conformity assessment;
Other matters deemed necessary by the Minister of Science and ICT for the procedures, methods, etc. for conformity assessment.
Article 77-14 (Procedures for reporting nonconformity)

When a person who has undergone conformity assessment becomes aware that the relevant equipment falls under any subparagraph of Article 58-11 (1) of the Act, the person shall report such fact to the Minister of Science and ICT within 5 days from the date the person becomes aware of the fact.

Pursuant to Article 58-11 (4) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT may impose a reduced level of administrative disposition on a person who has taken measures under paragraph (1) of that Article by up to 1/2 of the criteria for administrative disposition specified in Appendix 23; provided, where such administrative disposition falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Minister of Science and ICT may impose a reduction in the level of administrative disposition or exempt such person from the administrative disposition in accordance with the following classifications:
In the case of revocation: Disposition to suspend production, import, sale, or use for 4 months;
In the case of a corrective order and the suspension of production, import, sale, or use for 1 month: exemption.

Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), detailed matters necessary for reporting procedures, reduction in the level of administrative disposition or exemption from administrative disposition shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT.
Article 77-15 (Methods of indication)

Matters to be indicated pursuant to Article 58-12 (1) of the Act are as follows; provided, subparagraph 3 shall be indicated only where the Minister of Science and ICT has designated a center pursuant to Article 9-3 (1) of the Act: <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>
The time broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. becomes unusable and the fact that using it after the elapse of such time is the violation of the Act;
The dates manufacture, import, and sale of broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. are completed;
Matters regarding the center.
Paragraph (1) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the matters to be notified under Article 58-12 (2) of the Act.

Matters to be indicated under paragraph (1) shall be marked on the relevant equipment and the packaging of the equipment in a manner easily understandable by users, and a user guide describing the matters to be indicated shall be also included in the packaging.

Details necessary for the methods of indication and notification under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 85 (Disclosure of status of using radio frequencies)

The Minister of Science and ICT shall make public the status of using radio frequencies pursuant to Article 60 of the Act; provided, he or she need not disclose any information referred to in Article 9 (1) of the Official Information Disclosure Act . <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

The Minister of Science and ICT shall establish and operate an information system to disclose the status of using radio frequencies; and shall update the information system without delay, where the status of using radio frequencies is changed. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 12, 2017>

Detailed matters regarding the establishment and operation of an information system under paragraph (2) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Added on Dec. 12, 2017>
Article 86 (Technologies to be standardized and procedures)
Technologies using radio waves subject to standardization under Article 63 (2) of the Act are as follows:
Technologies concerning systems and services using radio waves;
Technologies concerning spectrum management and environment;
Other technologies using radio waves.

A person having interest in the standardization of technologies using radio waves may prepare a standard proposal on matters listed in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) and request the establishment or amendment thereof from the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Where the Minister of Science and ICT establishes, amends, or repeals standards for technologies using radio waves, he or she shall publicly notify the details thereof. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Procedures for the establishment, amendment, or repeal of standards under paragraph (3), and other necessary matters, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 87 (Guidance on and supervision of business affairs of the korea communications agency)

The Minister of Science and ICT shall guide and supervise the business affairs of the Agency pursuant to Article 66 (5) of the Act; and may issue instructions, dispositions, or orders to the Agency regarding its business affairs, if deemed necessary. <Amended on Dec. 9, 2008; Dec. 31, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 3, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

The Minister of Science and ICT may require the Agency to report on its business affairs, accounting, and property, or require subordinate public officials to inspect the books, documents, and other articles of the Agency. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Public officials conducting an inspection under paragraph (2) shall carry an identification indicating their authority and present it to interested persons.
Article 88 (Business projects of the association)
Cooperative activities among members;
Research, inspections, public relation activities, and publication to increase the use of radio waves and to heighten the recognition thereof;
Any of the following projects for efficiently using spectrum resources:
Surveying and analyzing demands for radio frequencies or technologies;
Creating a foundation to use radio frequencies or new technologies;
Any of the following projects for creating a business environment for the radio wave broadcasting industry:
Supporting the industrialization of radio wave broadcasting technology;
Supporting the distribution of broadcasting and communications equipment, broadcasting equipment, etc. for developing the radio wave broadcasting industry;
Supporting the entry of radio wave broadcasting technology, broadcasting and communications equipment, etc. into overseas markets;
Surveying the status of radio waves-related industries;
Surveying the status of broadcasting and communication equipment;
Developing and spreading technologies using radio waves;
Collecting, surveying, analyzing, and supplying information on technologies related to radio waves;
Conducting research on the standardization of technologies using radio waves;
Training experts in utilizing radio waves and broadcasting technology;
Deleted. <Jun. 21, 2016>
Business incidental to those referred to in subparagraphs 1, 2, 2-2, 2-3, 3, 3-2, 4 through 6, and 6-2, and other business necessary to attain the objectives of the Association.
Article 89 (Full or partial exemption from spectrum use fees)
"Radio station prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 67 (1) 6 of the Act means the following: <Amended on Jul. 26, 2010; Dec. 31, 2010; Jun. 21, 2016; Feb. 28, 2022>
An emergency station, experimental station, amateur station, standard radio frequency, and time signal station;

A radio station installed by the Korean Red Cross established under the Organization of the Republic of Korea National Red Cross Act and a radio station established to manage and operate the communication network for emergency medical service referred to in Article 25 (1) 6 of the Emergency Medical Service Act ;
A radio station falling under Article 90 (2) 1 or 2, the spectrum use fee to be imposed on which is less than 3,000 won, and a radio station falling under Appendix 7;
The following radio stations established in a tunnel, an urban rail transit (applicable only to those established underground), a basement of a building, etc.:
A radio station established to use communication services provided by a facility-based telecommunications business entity;
A satellite broadcasting auxiliary station established by a satellite digital multimedia broadcasting business entity;
A radio station for the prevention of disasters, such as flood forecast, and flood warning;
A radio station established by a facility-based telecommunications business entity, for the purpose of implementing the public duties of the State;
A radio station established by a facility-based telecommunications business entity, for the purpose of providing Internet services to farming and fishery villages via a satellite;

A radio station established by a non-profit corporation for providing education or conducting research that is determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, for the purpose of using the radio frequency spectrum of at least 28.9 GHz but not more than 29.5 GHz only within certain areas such as its building.
Full or partial exemption from the spectrum use fee under the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 67 (1) of the Act shall be classified as follows: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010>
Authorized persons of radio stations falling under Article 67 (1) 6 and 7 of the Act shall be fully exempted from the spectrum use fee;
30/100 of the spectrum use fee shall be reduced for authorized persons of radio stations falling under Article 67 (1) 4 or 5 of the Act.
Article 90 (Standards for calculating spectrum use fees)

Spectrum use fees for a radio station established by a facility-based telecommunications business entity to provide telecommunications services to subscribers pursuant to the proviso of Article 68 (1) of the Act shall be computed as stated in Appendix 8; provided, where telecommunications services are provided on a wholesale basis to another telecommunications service provider under Article 38 of the Telecommunications Business Act (only applicable to telecommunication service providers that are small and medium enterprises under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises or middle-standing enterprises under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Special Act on the Promotion of Growth and the Strengthening of Competitiveness of Middle-Standing Enterprises), the fees shall be calculated by subtracting the number of subscribers receiving such telecommunication services from such another telecommunication provider multiplied by the ratio according to the following subparagraphs from the number of subscribers shown in Appendix 8: <Amended on Mar. 26, 2024>
Where calculating spectrum use fees from January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2024: 100/100;
Where calculating spectrum use fees from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025: 80/100;
Where calculating spectrum use fees from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026: 50/100.
Spectrum use fees referred to in the main clause of Article 68 (1) of the Act shall be computed according to the following classification: <Amended on Jan. 24, 2017>
The standards for computing spectrum use fees for any of the following radio stations shall be as stated in Appendix 9:
Radio stations established by facility-based telecommunications business entities other than those referred to in paragraph (1);
Satellite broadcasting auxiliary stations established by satellite broadcasting business entities;
Radio stations using frequencies exclusively for the integrated public network (referring to frequencies 718 MHz to 728 MHz or frequencies 773 MHz to 783 MHz; hereinafter the same shall apply);
Standards for computing spectrum use fees for a radio station not falling under paragraph (1) and subparagraph 1 are as listed in Appendix 10;

Notwithstanding subparagraphs 1 and 2, spectrum use fees for a radio station used while in motion and an earth station established by a facility-based telecommunications business entity for lease purposes are as stated in Appendix 11.

Where the period for which spectrum use fees are to be imposed and collected pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2) does not exceed three months, the amount computed by dividing an amount computed by multiplying spectrum use fees for the relevant quarter by days for which spectrum use fees are to be imposed and collected, by the total days of the relevant quarter; provided, where the period for which spectrum use fees are to be imposed and collected from a radio station under paragraph (2) 3 does not exceed three months, no spectrum use fees shall be imposed and collected.

Notwithstanding paragraph (2) 1 and 2, no spectrum use fees shall be imposed on receiving facilities and stand-by facilities, and the period for suspension of operation under Article 25-2 (1) of the Act and the period for suspension of operation under Article 72 (3) of the Act shall not be counted in the days for imposition and collection of spectrum use fees. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010>
Article 91 (Period of collection of spectrum use fees)
Spectrum use fees shall be imposed and collected quarterly, and the quarterly collection period is as listed in Appendix 11-2. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010>

Notwithstanding paragraph (1), spectrum use fees shall be collected from a person who obtains authorization to establish a radio station in a quarter-year period during the collection period under paragraph (1), and spectrum use fees shall be collected from a person who closes a radio station upon closure of the radio station.

Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the authorized person of a radio station other than a radio station for which spectrum use fees are computed pursuant to Article 90 (1) may pay the full amount of annual spectrum use fees upfront. In such cases, a person who intends to pay annual spectrum use fees upfront shall file an application for lump-sum payment of spectrum use fees with the Minister of Science and ICT or the Korea Communications Commission. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>

Notwithstanding the latter part of paragraph (3), if the full amount of spectrum usage fees is paid in advance according to the notification by the Minister of Science and ICT or the Korea Communications Commission, an application for lump-sum payment of spectrum usage fees shall be deemed filed. <Added on Dec. 27, 2022>

Where a person intends to pay annual spectrum use fees upfront pursuant to paragraph (3), the person is entitled to a 10/100 reduction of the annual spectrum use fees payable. In such cases, one year means one year from the quarter following the quarter in which the filing date of an application for lump-sum payment of spectrum use fees falls. <Amended on Dec. 27, 2022>
Article 92 (Rate of surcharge on spectrum use fees)
Article 93 (Procedures for collecting spectrum use fees)

Procedures for collecting revenues under statutes or regulations governing the management of national funds shall apply mutatis mutandis to procedures for collecting spectrum use fees. In such cases, the notice of payment shall state the standards for computation of spectrum use fees, methods and time limit for filing an objection, etc.

Unless otherwise expressly prescribed in this Decree, matters necessary for the collection of spectrum use fees shall be determined, by public notice, by the Minister of Science and ICT after consultation with the Korea Communications Commission. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
Article 93-2 (Fees for filing applications for radio frequency assignment)
Article 94 Deleted. <Jun. 21, 2016>
Article 94-2 (Fees for filing applications for approval to use radio frequencies)
In cases of an application for approval: 12,000 won per radio frequency;
In cases of an application for modifying approved matters: 6,000 won per radio frequency;
In cases of an application for renewal: 6,000 won per radio frequency.
Article 95 (Fees for filing applications for authorization for radio stations)

A person who files an application for authorization for either a radio station or industrial, scientific, and medical equipment, an application for renewal of authorization, or an application for authorization for change as prescribed in Article 19 (1), 22 (1), or 58 (1) of the Act shall pay fees stated in Appendix 12. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010>

A person who files an application for authorization to change the purposes of facilities, counterpart to communications, matters of communications (matters of broadcasting in the case of a broadcasting station), call signs, call name, type of radio waves, or permitted working hours not accompanied by the change of facilities for a radio station, among the matters requiring authorization to change under the subparagraphs of Article 31 (4), shall pay 1,000 won as a fee, notwithstanding paragraph (1). <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010>
A person who files an application for authorization to simultaneously change matters specified under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall pay fees under paragraph (1).
Article 96 (Fees for inspection of radio stations)

A person who undergoes an inspection upon completion of construction, or a regular inspection or an occasional inspection of a radio station, industrial, scientific and medical equipment, etc. under Articles 24 (1), (4), (5), and (7) and 58 (3) of the Act shall pay a fee as specified in Appendix 13; provided, where a relevant facility is jointly used by at least two radio stations, a fee chargeable for inspection of one radio station shall be paid; and where each radio station has different antenna power, a fee for a radio station with the highest antenna power shall be paid. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Aug. 27, 2014; Jun. 21, 2016>

Fees referred to in paragraph (1) shall apply to all transmitting devices and receiving devices to be inspected; provided, where an inspection is conducted to grant authorization for change or upon receipt of a report on change under Articles 24 (1) and 58 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "modification inspection"), fees shall be calculated as follows according to the type of the radio station and the kind and scale of the relevant equipment: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2010; Jun. 21, 2016>

Where a modification inspection is conducted, 3/4 of the amount in the fees for modification inspection specified in Appendix 13 shall apply to the changed facilities for a transmitting device and a receiving device (excluding extension or replacement of devices);

Engaging in conversations with another examinee regarding the examination;
Exchanging answer sheets with another examinee;
Filling out the answer sheet by peeking at another examinee's answer sheet or examination paper;
Giving answers to another examinee or allowing him or her to peek at the answer sheet the relevant examine himself or herself/herself has prepared;
Carrying and using articles related to the contents of examination questions, or giving or receiving such articles to or from another examinee;
Filling out the answer sheet by receiving help from a person inside or outside of the place of examination;
Taking the examination after being informed of examination questions in advance;
Handing in the answer sheet by filling in another examinee’s name or application number on it;
Taking the examination for another person, or having another person sit for the examination;

Filling out the answer sheet using a communication device or electronic device [a mobile phone, portable personal digital assistant (PDA), portable multimedia player (PMP), portable computer, portable cassette, digital camera, MP3 player, portable game console, electronic dictionary, camera pen, or clock with additional functions in addition to the display of the time] or transmitting answers to another examinee during the examination;

ACT No.2280 19710213 RADIO WAVES ACT No.1913 19670414 RADIO WAVES ACT No.924 19620101 CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS 법령 이단보기 Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to prescribe matters relating to the efficient and safe use and control of radio waves to facilitate the promotion of the field relating to radio waves and serve to promote public welfare by facilitating the use of radio waves and the development of radio-wave technologies. <Amended on Jan. 20, 2015> [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 13, 2008] 법령 이단보기 Article 2 (Definitions) (1) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Jun. 13, 2008; Jul. 23, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 3, 2014; Jan. 20, 2015; Dec. 22, 2015; Jul. 26, 2017; Jun. 9, 2020> 1. The term "radio waves" means electromagnetic waves which propagate in space without any artificial guidance at radio frequencies within the range determined by the International Telecommunication Union; 2. The term "allocation of radio frequencies" means determining the use of specified radio frequencies; 3. The term "assignment of radio frequencies" means granting specific persons the right to use specified radio frequencies; 4. The term "designation of radio frequencies" means designating specific radio frequencies to be used by a radio station established after obtaining authorization or by filing a report thereon; 4-2. The term “approval for use of radio frequencies” means approving the use of specific radio frequencies for security or diplomatic purposes or for international or national events, etc.; 4-3. The term "withdrawal of radio frequencies" means withdrawing all or some of the radio frequencies assigned, designated, or approved for use; 4-4. The term "reallocation of radio frequencies" means assigning radio frequencies, designating radio frequencies, or granting approval for use of radio frequencies after withdrawing radio frequencies and in replacement thereof; 4-5. The term "joint use of radio frequencies" means use of radio frequencies within the same range by two or more frequency users without mutual exclusion; 5. The term "radio facilities" means electrical facilities capable of sending or receiving radio waves; 5-2. The term "radio communications" means sending or receiving information, such as all types of signs, signals, words, images and sounds, by using radio waves; 6. The term "radio station" means the integration of radio facilities, and persons who operate such radio facilities: Provided , That any radio station established only for the purpose of receiving broadcasts shall be excluded herefrom; 7. The term "operator" means any person who operates or performs installation and maintenance of radio facilities and holds a certificate of technical qualification issued under Article 70 (2); 8. The term "authorized person" means any person who establishes a radio station after obtaining authorization from, or filing a report with, the Minister of Science and ICT; 9. The term "broadcasting station" means a radio station established for the purpose of enabling the public to directly receive broadcasting signal; 10. The term "space station" means a radio station established in a satellite; 11. The term "earth station" means a radio station established on earth to communicate with a space station; 12. The term "satellite network" means the whole of a communications network (including satellite radio frequencies and satellite orbits; hereinafter the same shall apply) comprised of the space stations and the earth stations; 13. The term "satellite orbit" means the location or path of a space station; 14. The term "electromagnetic interference" means that electromagnetic waves emitted (referring to the propagation of electromagnetic energy in space) or conducted (referring to the flow of electromagnetic energy through power supply lines) by electromagnetic wave-generating equipment disturb the performance of other equipment; 15. The term "electromagnetic conformity" means when equipment that causes electromagnetic interference or is affected by electromagnetic waves, is in conformity with the technical requirements for electromagnetic interference and electromagnetic susceptibility under Article 47-3 (1); 16. The term "broadcasting and communications equipment" means devices, apparatuses, components or lines used for broadcasting and communications equipment; 17. The term "spectrum environment" means the overall conditions whereby electromagnetic waves are distributed, such as the intensity of radio waves and noise around the human body, machinery or radio facilities. (2) The definitions of terms used in this Act shall be governed by the Framework Act on Broadcasting Communications Development , except as otherwise expressly provided for in paragraph (1). <Added on Jul. 23, 2010> [Title Amended on Jun. 13 2008] 법령 이단보기 Article 3 (Facilitating Use of Spectrum Resources) The government shall formulate and implement policy measures necessary to facilitate the use of spectrum resources for the purpose of maximizing the use of limited spectrum resources for promoting the public welfare. [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 13, 2008] 법령 이단보기 Article 4 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2005> CHAPTER II SECURING SPECTRUM RESOURCES 법령 이단보기 Article 5 (Securing Spectrum Resources) (1) In order to secure spectrum resources, the Minister of Science and ICT shall formulate and implement the following policy measures and prepare a support scheme necessary for the implementation of such policy measures: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jan. 20, 2015; Dec. 22, 2015; Jul. 26, 2017> 1. Developing technologies for using new radio frequencies; 2. Enhancing efficiency in the use of the radio frequencies being used; 2-2. Developing technologies for the joint use of radio frequencies; 3. International registration of radio frequencies; 4. Consultations and coordination to remove and prevent radio wave interference between nations. (2) Necessary matters concerning radio frequencies subject to registration under paragraph (1) 3, registration fees, and registration procedures, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 13, 2008] 법령 이단보기 Article 6 (Enhancing Efficiency in Use of Spectrum Resources) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT shall, if necessary to facilitate the fair and efficient use of spectrum resources, implement the following: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017> 1. Alteration of allocation of radio frequencies; 2. Withdrawal of radio frequencies or reallocation of radio frequencies; 3. Conversion to new technical modes; 4. Sharing of radio frequencies. (2) The Minister of Science and ICT may investigate or confirm a current status of spectrum use, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, in cases where necessary for implementing matters falling under each subparagraph of paragraph (1). <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017> [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 13, 2008] 법령 이단보기 Article 6-2 (Withdrawal of Radio Frequencies or Reallocation of Radio Frequencies) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT may execute the withdrawal of radio frequencies or reallocation of radio frequencies under Article 6 (1) 2, in cases where falling under any of the following: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017> 1. Where the allocation of radio frequencies has been altered; 2. Where the actual levels of use of radio frequencies have been inactive or where it is necessary to elevate the efficient use of frequency through a readjustment of frequency band. (2) Necessary matters concerning a withdrawal of radio frequencies or procedures for reallocation of radio frequencies under paragraph (1), standards to determine the actual levels of use of radio frequencies, and requisite, etc. for readjustment of frequency bands shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. (3) Where radio frequencies need to be newly allocated, withdrawn, or relocated, it shall be deliberated by a frequency deliberation committee chaired by the Minister of the Office for Government Policy Coordination. <Added on Mar. 23, 2013> (4) Matters necessary for the composition, operation, etc. of the frequency deliberation committee under paragraph (3) shall be determined by Presidential Decree. <Added on Mar. 23, 2013> [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 13, 2008] 법령 이단보기 Article 6-3 (Joint Use of Radio Frequencies) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT may require a person granted the assignment, designation, or approval for use of, radio frequencies to fully or partially provide radio frequencies for the joint use thereof: Provided , That he or she shall agree with the Korea Communications Commission on the radio frequencies used for the broadcasting business under Article 6-4 . <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017> (2) The Minister of Science and ICT shall determine and publicly announce the standards for the joint use of radio frequencies, including the scope and conditions of, and procedures and methods for joint use of radio frequencies: Provided , That he or she shall agree with the Korea Communications Commission on the radio frequencies used for the broadcasting business under Article 6-4 . <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017> [This Article Added on Jan. 20, 2015] [Previous Article 6-3 moved to Article 6-4 <Jan. 20, 2015>] 법령 이단보기 Article 6-4 (Management of Broadcasting Radio Frequencies) Radio frequencies used in the broadcasting business provided for in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Broadcasting Act shall be managed by the Korea Communications Commission. [This Article Added on Mar. 23, 2013] [Moved from Article 6-3 <Jan. 20, 2015>] 법령 이단보기 Article 7 (Compensation for Loss from Withdrawal of Radio Frequencies or Relocation of Radio Frequencies) (1) In implementing withdrawal of radio frequencies or reallocation of radio frequencies under Article 6-2 , the Minister of Science and ICT shall compensate for any loss incurred in the ordinary course of business by the relevant authorized person and a person who has obtained approval for use of radio frequency under Article 18-2 (3) (hereinafter referred to as "authorized person, etc."): Provided , That the same shall not apply to the following cases: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 3, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017> 1. Where withdrawal of radio frequencies or reallocation of radio frequencies is implemented at the request of the authorized person, etc.; 2. Where the International Telecommunication Union has altered the allocation of a radio frequency, following the alteration of international allocation of a radio frequency that is to be commonly adopted by all nations; 3. Where using a frequency which is set for secondary services (referring to services that shall provide protection to, and not claim protection from, a primary service in operating their frequencies; hereinafter the same shall apply). (2) Where the Minister of Science and ICT compensates for any loss under the main clause, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of paragraph (1), he or she may collect the amount of compensation under paragraph (1) from the person who has been newly allocated with radio frequencies or the person who has newly obtained designation of radio frequencies or approval for use of radio frequencies (hereinafter referred to as "new user") for the relevant radio frequencies. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017> (3) When the Minister of Science and ICT intends to determine the amount of compensation for loss under paragraph (1), it shall seek opinions from the relevant authorized person, etc. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013;
